related_resources.reason: Primary chronology; nobility, Scania, Copenhagen, eclipse, Leipzig, 1566 duel at Rostock, Hven instruments, fief obligations, court change and Prague. Danish scholarship preferred where popular dates conflict.
Biography and publication history; Danish court, Hven scientific/cultural institution, printers, paper mill, exile and Kepler.
Detailed source for royal patronage, instrument engineering, observer/assistant roles, Hven, Wandsbek and printing of the Mechanica in 1598.

Family and foster household, education, conjunction tables, Kirsten and children, Sophie, observatory personnel, court conflict, technical legacy. Some traditional nose claims superseded by 2010 exhumation.

Observational program, calibration, systematic planet positions, observational record, publication, Kepler and later data ownership. Reports Wittenberg for duel; prefer primary Danish/Rostock for location.
Nova and comet, diurnal parallax, Tychonic model, lunar/planetary observations, precision instruments; some conflicting dates are not used.
Astronomical instruments, 1572 nova, 1577 comet and beyond-lunar inference, Italian travel and technical milestones.
1566 duel location, studies and historical milestones. Its statement that mercury caused death is outdated; the exhumation report controls that claim.
University attendance, eclipse interest, learning travels and Hven. Its outdated theory of mercury death is not used.
Sophie Brahe own astronomy, chemistry, horticulture and genealogy, 1573 work with brother, 1590 Hven visits, uncertain birth year and scholarly limits.
2010 exhumation, measured mercury concentrations incompatible with mercury-poisoning death, copper-zinc traces supporting brass nasal prosthesis. Does not identify exact medical cause.
Posthumous ownership and Kepler contract of 1604; 1627 tables, elliptic planetary theory and numerical prediction.
November 1572 first-person recollection and modern supernova framing; use only short paraphrase, no unsupported historical dialogue.
Abstract argues that some Mars opposition table entries were revised in alignment with a model. Companion-only nuanced note; no claims about all data or individual motive.

birth.label: Born 14 December at Knutstorp in Scania, then Denmark, now Sweden

foster_household.label: Raised in uncle Jørgen Brahe and Inger Oxe household, approximate childhood date

copenhagen.label: Begins University of Copenhagen studies in April, aged twelve

solar_eclipse.label: 21 August partial solar eclipse prompts sustained interest in prediction

leipzig.label: Leipzig education, with Anders Sørensen Vedel as companion and tutor

planet_conjunction.label: August Jupiter–Saturn conjunction exposes tabular discrepancies

uncle_death.label: Death of Jørgen Brahe during early travels

duel.label: 29 December duel in Rostock; part of nose lost

augsburg_instruments.label: Builds major quadrant and celestial globe with local instrument patrons in Augsburg

father_death.label: Otte Brahe dies; Tycho based again in Scania

partnership.label: Long partnership with Kirsten Jørgensdatter begins, approximate start

nova.label: 11 November observes bright new star in Cassiopeia

nova_book.label: Publishes De nova stella; other observers also saw the object

copenhagen_lecture.label: Offers course of astronomical lectures in Copenhagen

sophie_collaboration.label: Works with sister Sophie Brahe, whose scientific pursuits also independent

hven_grant.label: Frederick II grants Hven fief and major patronage for observatory

uraniborg.label: Construction of Uraniborg begins; institution operates through 1597

comet.label: Observes great comet and derives large distance from small parallax

stjerneborg.label: Builds partly underground Stjerneborg to stabilize observations

tycho_system.label: Develops and publishes geoheliocentric Tychonic planetary arrangement; approximate development

printing.label: Printing press and paper-mill investments on Hven

king_death.label: Frederick II dies, changing court patronage and regency context

court_change.label: Christian IV crowned; earlier disputes over patronage, obligations and tenants intensify

leave_hven.label: Leaves Hven with household and parts of research program

mechanica.label: Completes richly illustrated Astronomiae instauratae mechanica at Wandsbek

prague.label: Arrives in Prague with imperial patron Rudolf II; work also at Benátky

kepler.label: Johannes Kepler joins work on Mars, alongside others including Longomontanus

death.label: Dies 24 October in Prague; exact illness contested

kepler_book.label: Kepler publishes Astronomia nova with new laws based on Mars observations (posthumous context)

rudolphine_tables.label: Kepler publishes Rudolphine Tables using Tycho data and elliptic astronomy (posthumous)

stellar_parallax.label: Nineteenth-century measurement of annual stellar parallax (posthumous scientific context)

exhumation.label: Exhumation and later analyses rule out mercury death and identify copper-zinc residue (modern research)

mars_reassessment.label: Published historical reanalysis challenges neutrality of some tabulated Mars oppositions (interpretive context)
